Subject: Evaluating Dedicated GPU pool options for inference workloads

Hi Soojin,

We're getting into procurement for a committed dedicated pool for our inference platform. Primary questions for a first pass:

- Rough perf/$ and memory trade-offs between A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), and L40S (48GB) for transformer decoding workloads (mainly 8k contexts, multi-model: one 30B, a few 7B models).
- If we commit to an annual reserved capacity (expressed as x GPUs equivalent), what typical discount tiers do you offer? Any add-on for strict throughput / SLO guarantees?
- Can Redwood support a mixed pool (H100 + L40S) with routing policies so latency-critical traffic goes to H100s and cost-batch traffic goes to L40S? Any limitations?

We want a short proposal and a spreadsheet we can share with procurement. Can you include assumptions (batch size distribution, token/sec targets) so we can size?

Thanks — if useful, we can do a 30-min call next week.

Alex
Procurement, NimbusAI

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a scoped pricing workbook and a throughput model (see attachments) and outlining the high-level tradeoffs below. Happy to jump on a call — I’m available Wed/Thu next week.

Quick summary (high-level):
- H100 (80GB) — best perf/$ for large-context, multi-model setups where you need fewer concurrent copies (larger KV caches, bigger batch headroom). Expect ~1.8–2.2x decoding throughput vs A100 for long sequences; effective perf/$ often wins once utilization >55%.
- A100 (40GB) — steady performer for mid-size models; lower unit cost but more replicas required for memory-heavy models which increases orchestration overhead. Good sweet spot for 30B single-model workloads where batch sizes are modest.
- L40S (48GB) — optimized for cost-sensitive, high-concurrency inference when models are quantized. Perf is lower than H100 per card, but cost per GPU is substantially lower; ideal as a second tier for non-latency-critical requests.

Recommended packaging options (examples):
- Small commit (3-month) — 8 GPU equivalent baseline: 7% discount off list; throughput advisory only (no SLA).
- Standard commit (annual) — 32 GPU equivalent baseline: 18% discount; 99.95% uptime SLA + throughput budget and priority routing.
- Enterprise commit (annual, 2-yr) — 64+ GPU baseline: 28% discount; 99.97% SLA, dedicated support, custom fallback/overprovision windows.

Mixed-pool guidance:
- We support mixed pools with policy routing. Typical pattern: reserve 25–40% H100s for latency-critical endpoints and 60–75% L40S for background/batched traffic. Intelligent routing (latency tags + model pinning) ensures deterministic fallbacks.
- Considerations: KV cache warm-start between heterogeneous cards is not shared; moving an active session between card types may incur rewarm latency. We recommend keep-alive affinity for latency-SLO traffic.

Sizing assumptions I used are included in the CSV: average token length, percent synchronous calls, p99 latency target 400ms, and 50% off-peak traffic. Please review and tell me the three metrics you care most about (tokens/sec, p50 latency, p95 latency) and I’ll tune the model.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_NimbusAI_v2.xlsx, Throughput_Sizing_Model_Nimbus.csv

Best,

Thanks, Soojin — that helps. A couple of clarifying items from Priya and me after we ran the CSV with our traffic profile:

- Our steady-state target is ~75k tokens/sec across the fleet with p95 latency < 500ms. Peak bursts are 2–3x for short windows.
- We plan to quantize a subset of 7B models to 4-bit; the 30B will remain FP16. Memory headroom is important for that mix.
- Can you quantify perf/$ in your spreadsheet as relative cost per 1M tokens served (run both 40GB A100 and 80GB H100 columns)?

Also: can Redwood include an option for a 12-month commit with a +5% discount if paid upfront? Procurement will likely prefer single-year commitments they can amortize.

Alex

Alex / team — looping in product because you raised a couple of good platform-specific questions. A few product notes to add:

- H100 variants: our H100 fleet is mixed across 80GB SXM and newer 80GB PCIe cards. For very long KV caches we prefer SXM (slightly better sustained memory bandwidth). We can mark which physical GPUs are SXM if you need consistency for benchmarking.
- Mixed pools: routing supports model-level pinning and latency tags. To minimize cache re-warm, we recommend a small H100-only routing reservation per latency-critical endpoint.
- Throughput guarantees: for annual commits we provide a reserved throughput SLA expressed as "tokens/min reserved" with burst credit buckets. This is in the SOW appendix if you move forward.

Soojin — I updated the pricing workbook to include the per-1M-token cost for A100/H100/L40S (tab: unit_econ). Also created an alternative '12mo upfront' tab that applies your +5% referral.

If Nimbus wants to proceed, next steps we typically suggest: 1) agree on pool mix and commit level, 2) sign SOW (DocuSign link below), 3) 2-week onboarding runbook + benchmark window.
